title: Flip-flops and latches (sequential logic)
summary: Flip-flops are bistable circuits (1-bit memory). Types: SR latch (set/reset), D latch (data), D flip-flop (edge-triggered), JK flip-flop (toggle), T flip-flop (toggle). Latches are level-sensitive; flip-flops are edge-triggered. Setup time, hold time, and clock-to-Q delay are key timing parameters.

structure.meaning: Set (S=1, R=0): Q=1. Reset (S=0, R=1): Q=0. Invalid: S=1, R=1. (S=R=0: hold.)
When E=1 (enable): Q=D. When E=0: hold. Transparent latch.
On rising edge of CLK: Q=D. Edge-triggered. Master-slave or pulse-triggered.
J=K=0: hold. J=1, K=0: set. J=0, K=1: reset. J=K=1: toggle.
T=0: hold. T=1: toggle. (T flip-flop = JK with J=K=T.)
Minimum time data must be stable before the clock edge.
Minimum time data must be stable after the clock edge.
Time from clock edge to output change.

notes: D flip-flop is the most common (used in registers, pipelines).
JK flip-flop is universal (can implement any flip-flop type).
Edge-triggered flip-flops are preferred over latches in synchronous design.
Flip-flops are the basis of registers, counters, state machines, and pipelines.
